about.title: Fillmore Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Fillmore's mix of state highway traffic on Rt 126, cross-town flow along Ventura Street and A Street, and Friday evening congestion between 5 and 7 p.m. creates real opportunities for collisions. Recent figures show 58 injury crashes and 90 people hurt in a single year here, a reminder that these outcomes touch real neighbors, not just statistics. If you were injured, what you do in the first days matters: California law gives you a limited window to act, insurers may ask for a recorded statement early, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, or witness contact information can disappear fast. LawProactive doesn't practice law or charge you anything. We simply connect you with an independent personal injury attorney working on contingency, so you can focus on recovery while someone experienced handles the insurance back-and-forth on your behalf.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before You Talk to the Insurer

items.title: California's Clock Is Ticking
items.desc: You generally have two years to file a car accident claim in California, but if a government vehicle or road hazard was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Acting sooner protects your options later.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California allows recovery even if you're partly at fault, but your share of blame reduces your payout. An early recorded statement to the other driver's insurer can be used to inflate your share of fault, so it's worth having guidance first.

items.title: No Cap Means Your Full Story Matters
items.desc: California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so documenting how the crash affected your daily life in Fillmore can matter as much as your medical bills.

items.question: Do I have to give the insurance company a recorded statement after my crash on Ventura Street?
items.answer: No, you're not required to give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurer, and it's often safer not to until you've spoken with an attorney. Statements can be used later to shift blame onto you under California's comparative fault rules. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Fillmore car accident?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. That window can be much shorter, sometimes six months, if a government entity, like Ventura County or Caltrans, was involved in causing the crash. It's best to get advice early rather than risk missing a deadline.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for the collision?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible, though your compensation is reduced by your percentage of fault. This makes it important to have someone evaluate the evidence early, especially at busier Fillmore intersections along Rt 126 or A Street where fault can be contested.
